records.Concise description: A Bitcoin payment ecosystem that evolved from a self-custodial Lightning wallet into a major SDK platform for embedding non-custodial Lightning, Liquid and Spark-based payments.
records.Deeper researched summary: Breez's canonical role now spans its original consumer-wallet lineage and the Breez SDK. Current SDK implementations include Spark and Liquid architectures that let third-party applications offer instant Bitcoin payments while keeping user-side key control in standard client deployments. The exact trust model depends on the chosen implementation: Lightning, Spark and Liquid are not interchangeable security models.
records.Launch / history: Breez launched its Lightning wallet work in the late 2010s. By 2025–2026 the project's center of gravity had shifted strongly toward Breez SDK integrations, including Spark and Liquid implementations.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: Breez is a key wallet-infrastructure entity because many end-user apps can gain Bitcoin payment capability through its SDK without Breez itself being the visible wallet brand.
Important technical or cultural characte: Non-custodial client designs in standard deployments
Lightning addresses / LNURL / BOLT support depending implementation
records.Verification basis: Current 2026 Breez SDK documentation and project repositories verify active development and the multiple implementation models.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not publish a single undifferentiated 'Breez custody model' for every integration; SDK deployment and selected backend materially affect trust assumptions.
Treat the legacy consumer wallet and current SDK platform as one canonical Breez ecosystem profile, not duplicate entities.

records.Concise description: An open-source mobile wallet that runs a full non-custodial LND node on the user's device and exposes direct Lightning channel control.
records.Deeper researched summary: Blixt runs LND with Neutrino-style lightweight Bitcoin synchronization directly on a mobile device. Users control keys and channels, can open channels manually, and can use Blixt's LSP automation if desired. Its architecture is more node-like than most consumer Lightning wallets and therefore exposes more operational detail and local storage requirements.
records.Launch / history: Blixt emerged around 2020 and remained actively maintained; Android release 0.9.0 shipped in February 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: It is a distinctive mobile wallet because it puts a genuine Lightning node and channel manager on the phone rather than delegating channel state to a custodial account.
Important technical or cultural characte: Android is the clearest current production platform
No centralized transaction backend required for normal wallet operation
records.Verification basis: Current first-party feature documentation and 2026 release activity verify the embedded-node design and active lifecycle.
Research notes / uncertainties: iOS availability/testing status changes over time; the registry does not make an unqualified 2026 iOS production-availability claim.
Running a Lightning node on mobile creates backup/channel-state and resource considerations that should not be hidden in beginner copy.

records.Concise description: A self-custodial mobile wallet presenting on-chain and Lightning payments through one balance, backed by a 2-of-2 key architecture and an Emergency Kit.
records.Deeper researched summary: Muun uses a 2-of-2 spending architecture in which the phone holds one key while the exported Emergency Kit contains the material needed for independent recovery, including both keys and output descriptors. It deliberately does not use a conventional mnemonic as its main recovery format. Lightning payments are abstracted into the same balance and may involve submarine-swap-style transaction mechanisms rather than a user-managed Lightning channel balance.
Creators / founders: Dario Sneidermanis — co-founder / public project lead
records.Launch / history: Founded in the late 2010s and developed continuously as a mobile Bitcoin/Lightning wallet; the mobile apps received 2026 updates.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: It is a notable example of a wallet optimizing recovery and payment abstraction rather than exposing distinct on-chain and Lightning balances to users.
Important technical or cultural characte: Emergency Kit contains private-key/recovery material and output descriptors
No conventional BIP39 mnemonic as primary backup
records.Verification basis: Current Muun first-party site and app activity verify custody model, platforms, 2-of-2 structure and Emergency Kit approach.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not describe Muun as a conventional channel-managing Lightning wallet; its payment abstraction differs from wallets where the user directly manages Lightning channels.
The server co-signing role does not alone make Muun custodial because the Emergency Kit provides an independent recovery/spend path; this should be explained precisely.

records.Concise description: An open-source Lightning wallet ecosystem centered on Alby Hub, Nostr Wallet Connect, browser integration and the Alby Go mobile interface.
records.Deeper researched summary: Alby has evolved from a browser Lightning wallet toward a modular system. Alby Hub is a self-custodial Lightning node/wallet, while the browser extension and Alby Go can act as interfaces to Hub or other Nostr Wallet Connect-compatible wallets. The optional Alby web account can add a Lightning address and account services, but should not be confused with custody of funds in a user's Hub.
records.Launch / history: Alby emerged in the early 2020s as a browser Lightning wallet and expanded into Alby Hub, Alby Go and Nostr Wallet Connect infrastructure.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: Alby helped make permissioned wallet-to-application connections a first-class part of the Lightning/Nostr ecosystem and provides a clear separation between a self-hosted wallet backend and multiple user interfaces.
Important technical or cultural characte: Alby Go on iOS and Android
Lightning address integration through optional Alby Account

Official sources.label: Alby Hub self-custodial wallet / account linking

records.Verification basis: Current Alby Hub, NWC and Alby Go documentation verifies the present ecosystem structure and self-custodial Hub model.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not call the browser extension itself the custodian; it can be an interface to different wallet backends.
An Alby Account's Lightning-address/web services are separable from custody of funds in a self-hosted Alby Hub.
